metadata.summary: Carlos Alcaraz won his fourth title of an injury-disrupted season as he defeated Alex de Minaur in the Erste Bank Open final in Vienna.
metadata.content: Carlos Alcaraz: Spaniard seals Erste Bank Open victory in Vienna as he defeats Alex de Minaur | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Carlos Alcaraz: Spaniard seals Erste Bank Open victory in Vienna as he defeats Alex de Minaur Carlos Alcaraz picks up his fourth title of 2026 with 6-1 6-4 victory; world No 3 defeats Alex de Minaur for seventh match in a row; watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports from Monday Sunday 1 November 2026 15:32, UK Image: Carlos Alcaraz beat Alex de Minaur to ‌win the Erste Bank Open in Vienna on Sunday Carlos Alcaraz won his fourth title of an injury-disrupted season as he defeated Alex de Minaur in the Erste Bank Open final in Vienna. The Spaniard, who missed five months of the year with a wrist issue, powered to a 6-1 6-4 win against world No 10 Minaur in the indoor hard-court event. World No 3 Alcaraz delivered a high-quality, 97-minute display to overwhelm De Minaur and secure the title without dropping a set across his five matches. messages.text: Britain's Dart wins maiden WTA Tour title at Guangzhou Open

metadata.summary: Harriet Dart beat Lilli Tagger to win her first WTA Tour title at the Guangzhou Open.
metadata.content: Harriet Dart beats Austria's Lilli Tagger to win first WTA Tour title at Guangzhou Open | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Harriet Dart beats Austria's Lilli Tagger to win first WTA Tour title at Guangzhou Open Britain's Harriet Dart defeats Lilli Tagger to take home her first WTA title at the Guangzhou Open on Sunday; You can watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports from Monday November 2 Sunday 1 November 2026 13:17, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Guangzhou Open final between Harriet Dart and Lilli Tagger Harriet Dart beat Lilli Tagger to win her first WTA Tour title at the Guangzhou Open. Dart, who saved three match points in her semi-final win over Sun Xinran to reach her first Tour-level final, edged a thrilling match against the 18-year-old from Austria 4-6 6-3 6-4. Qualifier Dart, the British No 5 who is coached by former Wimbledon champion and Sky Sports analyst Marion Bartoli, dropped serve in the opening game and had to save a break point in her next service game before finally getting on the board. messages.text: England out of World Cup after Tonga edge out Samoa

metadata.summary: England's elimination from the World Cup was confirmed after Tonga beat Samoa 20-18 in the final group match.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: England's elimination confirmed after Tonga beat Samoa in the final group match | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rugby League World Cup: England's elimination confirmed after Tonga beat Samoa in the final group match England suffer historic group-stage exit at the Rugby League World Cup with Tonga unable to defeat Samoa by more than 46 points; Tonga will play New Zealand in the last four, while Samoa will face Australia in a repeat of the 2022 final Sunday 1 November 2026 12:39, UK Image: Robert Toia of Tonga celebrates scoring against Samoa at CommBank Stadium England's elimination from the World Cup was confirmed after Tonga beat Samoa 20-18 in the final group match. England sealed a 34-12 victory against Papua New Guinea on Friday but needed to win by a big margin to give themselves a chance of leapfrogging Samoa in Pool B and C and advancing to the semi-finals on points difference. Brian McDermott's side's hopes rested on Tonga to win by more than 46 points to reach the last four for the seventh successive tournament. messages.text: USA's Novak builds six-shot lead after three rounds at Mexico Open

metadata.summary: Andrew Novak built a comfortable lead at the turn and then poured it on by going five under par on the first five holes of the back nine on his way to a nine-under 62 as he built a six-shot lead at the Mexico Open.
metadata.content: Mexico Open: Andrew Novak builds six-shot lead after three rounds at PGA Tour event following stellar Saturday display | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mexico Open: Andrew Novak builds six-shot lead after three rounds at PGA Tour event following stellar Saturday display Saturday's third round of the Mexico Open sees the USA's Andrew Novak build six-shot lead at PGA Tour event; France's Matthieu Pavon currently sits second in standings; watch live coverage of the final round of the Mexico Open from 8pm on Sky Sports Golf on Sunday Sunday 1 November 2026 00:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the third round of the Mexico Open Andrew Novak built a comfortable lead at the turn and then poured it on by going five under par on the first five holes of the back nine on his way to a nine-under 62 as he built a six-shot lead at the Mexico Open. About the only thing Novak did wrong at Vidanta Vallarta was losing the handle on a club twirl at the par-five 12th while admiring a 279-yard shot that settled 20 feet away for an eagle. That was part of his sublime stretch of three birdies and an eagle that extended his lead to seven shots. It was such a great day for Novak that even when he had a lie in the rough with a golf ball well below his feet, he hammered that out to six feet on the 14th for a birdie. The Gunners had 27 shots in total at the Emirates but were left frustrated by a stoic defensive performance from Villa, who sat deep to preserve their lead after Chasity Grant scored with their only shot of the game in the 25th minute.
